findings.description: The AI-1 fix for the font size memory leak was incorrectly applied. Commit d52dc5e correctly added `allButtons.clear()` at the start of `populateKeyGrid()` to prevent detached button accumulation on shift toggle. Commit 144b6fb (the fix round) REMOVED this line, claiming to 'fix' the bug by 'removing allButtons.clear() from populateKeyGrid()'. This reintroduces and worsens the memory leak: every shift toggle (line 236) or shifted letter press (line 214) calls `populateKeyGrid()` which adds ~30 new Button instances to `allButtons` via `styledButton()` (line 335) without ever clearing the old detached ones. `changeFontSize()` (line 317) then iterates over all accumulated buttons including detached ones. The correct fix requires either (a) not tracking buttons in a list at all (like FloatingKeyboardOverlay's rebuildContent approach), or (b) clearing and rebuilding ALL button rows when shift toggles, not just the key grid.

REVIEW_FINDINGS.json is a review artifact that was added in commit 144b6fb and should not be committed to the repository. The REV-1 finding from the prior review round explicitly requested deletion of the stray 'review_findings.json' artifact, but the fix round only deleted a lowercase 'review_findings.json' file while this uppercase 'REVIEW_FINDINGS.json' remains. This file contains review metadata, not source code, and pollutes the repository.

Core focus-reclaim fix correctly implements the user intent: onAccessibilityEvent (line 230) and startFocusWatchdog (line 983) now use `view.hasWindowFocus()` instead of `view.isFocused`; FOCUS_WATCHDOG_INTERVAL_MS tightened from 2000ms to 150ms (line 1261); MotionCaptureView.onWindowFocusChanged (lines 1231-1238) provides immediate focus reclaim. All changes match the stated intent exactly and address the reported button unreliability root cause.

MotionCaptureView comment (line 1218-1223) claims digital buttons route through the focused capture view as the primary path ('the a11y onKeyEvent path loses the race'), but onKeyEvent (line 311) returns true for all mapped keys, consuming them before MotionCaptureView ever sees them. The user intent states digital buttons are 'dispatched through the same MotionCaptureView', but the a11y filter handles them instead. This means the focus-reclaim watchdog (which only protects MotionCaptureView) may not benefit the a11y filter path for digital buttons (A/B/X/Y/L1/R1). If the a11y filter path is the actual delivery mechanism for digital buttons, focus loss on MotionCaptureView wouldn't affect them — but the reported bug was exactly that digital buttons failed intermittently. Needs clarification on which path is authoritative for digital buttons.

testing_summary: Build compiles successfully. No test suite exists in this repo; the focus fix cannot be live-verified in this sandboxed environment (no KVM/emulator, no physical gamepad) — same limitation acknowledged in prior runs. The AI-1 regression was verified by code inspection: populateKeyGrid() no longer clears allButtons, causing detached Button accumulation on every shift toggle.
risk_rationale: The core focus fix is correct and low-risk, but the fix round introduced a regression (AI-1) that worsens a memory leak in AIInputMethodService, and a stray review artifact (REVIEW_FINDINGS.json) was committed. Additionally, there's an architecture mismatch between the MotionCaptureView comment and actual key event routing that could mean the focus fix doesn't fully address digital button reliability. Pre-existing design decisions (auth token, profile migration, double-press cancel, preset mismatches) remain unchanged from prior rounds.
